{{nihongo|'''Kokuzō Shrine'''|国造神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Higo Province]].

=== History and origin ===
The {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} lists four shrines in {{ill|Higo Province|bar|Provinz Higo|ca|Província de Higo|cs|Provincie Higo|de|Provinz Higo|es|Provincia de Higo|fa|ولایت هیگو|fi|Higon provinssi|fr|Higo|gl|Provincia de Higo|he|היגו (פרובינציה)|hu|Higo tartomány|id|Provinsi Higo|it|Higo|ja|肥後国|ko|히고국|lt|Higo žemė|nl|Higo (provincie)|pt|Província de Higo|ru|Хиго (провинция)|simple|Higo Province|sk|Higo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Хиго|tr|Higo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Хіґо|wuu|肥后国|zh|肥後國|zh_min_nan|Higo-kok|zh_yue|肥後國|qid=Q259705}} (Takeiwatatsu-no-Mikoto Shrine = present {{ill|Aso Shrine|fi|Aso-jinja|fr|Aso-jinja|ja|阿蘇神社|ko|아소 신사|simple|Aso Shrine|zh|阿蘇神社|qid=Q715639}}, Asohime Shrine = present Aso Shrine, Kokuzō Shrine, and {{ill|Hikino Shrine|ja|疋野神社|qid=Q17224057}}). Kokuzō Shrine is one of these four and is one of the oldest shrines in Kumamoto Prefecture. According to ''Higo no Kuni-shi'', in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, Hayamikatama-no-Mikoto was appointed Higo no Kuni no Miyatsuko, and in {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ar|الإمبراطور كيكو|arz|الامبراطور كيكو|azb|کیکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Keikō|cs|Keikó|de|Keikō|es|Keikō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیکو|fr|Keikō (empereur)|hr|Keikō|hu|Keikó japán császár|id|Kaisar Keikō|it|Keikō|ja|景行天皇|ka|კეიკო|ko|게이코 천황|nds|Keikō|nl|Keiko (keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|simple|Emperor Keikō|sl|Cesar Kejko|sv|Keiko (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเคโก|tl|Emperador Keikō|tr|Keikō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейко|uz|Imperator Keikō|vi|Thiên hoàng Keikō|yo|Emperor Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723}} 18 ({{ill|AD 88|Q24844|qid=Q24844}}), Kokuzō Shrine was repaired and rituals were organized<ref>''Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 44: Place Names of Kumamoto Prefecture'', Heibonsha, 1985, p.310</ref>.

With his father, Aso Shrine's principal deity {{ill|Takeiwatatsu-no-Mikoto|Q10888904|qid=Q10888904}}, he is said to have developed the Aso area and taught agriculture and afforestation. The principal deity is '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hayamikatama-no-Mikoto}}''' (according to ''{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|Q133833194|qid=Q133833194}}'', the first '''{{ill|Aso Kuni no Miyatsuko|Q56347021|qid=Q56347021}}'''), and together with his consort and sons, four deities are enshrined<ref>Editorial Committee of Kadokawa Place Names Dictionary (ed.), ''Kadokawa Place Names Dictionary 43 Kumamoto Prefecture'', Kadokawa Shoten, 1987, p.481</ref>.

The current shrine buildings were built in {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 12 ({{ill|1672|Q7614|qid=Q7614}}) by {{ill|Hosokawa Tsunatoshi|Q11605971|qid=Q11605971}}, third lord of the {{ill|Kumamoto Domain|Q1194248|qid=Q1194248|lt=Higo Kumamoto Domain}}<ref>Kadokawa Place Names Dictionary 43 Kumamoto Prefecture, Kadokawa Shoten, 1987, p.1297</ref>. It became a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}} in Meiji 5.

About 60 m west of the torii are the '''Kamimikura Kofun''', regarded as the tomb of the enshrined deity Hayamikatama-no-Mikoto, and the '''Shimomikura Kofun''', regarded as the tomb of his consort Amiya-hime-no-Mikoto. These are late-6th-century {{ill|Round Kofun|Q11394747|qid=Q11394747}} with {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|Q11543435|qid=Q11543435}}, built of huge {{ill|Andesite|Q181908|qid=Q181908}} blocks and cut Aso lava stone, and are representative megalithic kofun of Kumamoto.

=== Teno no Sugi ===
[[ファイル:Tenonosugi.jpg|thumb|right|240px|Preserved remains of Teno no Sugi]]
A giant cedar known as "{{ill|Teno No Sugi|ja|手野のスギ|qid=Q17217752}}" once stood in the precincts<ref name="Natural monument encyclopedia 116">''Natural Monument Encyclopedia'', p.116.</ref><ref name="Japan natural monuments 151">''Natural Monuments of Japan'', p.151.</ref>. It was designated a national natural monument on December 9, 1924, under the then Historic Sites, Places of Scenic Beauty and Natural Monuments Preservation Law<ref>Ministry of Home Affairs Notice No. 777, Taishō 13</ref>. It broke in Typhoon No. 19 (the "Apple Typhoon") on September 27, 1991, and in 2000 the Council for Cultural Affairs recommended de-designation<ref name="Natural monument encyclopedia 116"/><ref name="Japan natural monuments 151"/><ref name="de-designation (Agency for Cultural Affairs)">[https://web.archive.org/web/20060111191246/http://www.bunka.go.jp/1hogo/main.asp%7B0fl=show&id=1000007342&clc=1000011213&cmc=1000007006&cli=1000007317&cmi=1000007325%7B9.html Historic Sites / Scenic Places / Natural Monuments (May 2000)] Agency for Cultural Affairs website, viewed 2013-06-10.</ref>, and it was officially de-designated on September 6, 2000<ref>Ministry of Education Notice No. 150, 2000</ref>.

{{Main|Teno no Sugi}}

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Hayamikatama-no-Mikoto - son of Aso Shrine principal deity Takeiwatatsu-no-Mikoto. Aso Kuni no Miyatsuko Ōkami. Enshrined at the 11th shrine of Aso Shrine.
* Amiya-hime-no-Mikoto - consort of Hayamikatama-no-Mikoto. Also called Kamachi-hime-no-Mikoto; sea deity goddess. Principal deity of {{ill|Konoura Shrine|Q11643225|qid=Q11643225}}.
* Takahashi-no-Kami - second son of Hayamikatama-no-Mikoto.
* Hinomiya-no-Kami - third son of Hayamikatama-no-Mikoto.
